item.stem:
Ritu looks at the diagram. Straight lines $\ell$ and $m$ lie on the same flat page. Transversal $t$ meets them. One marked corresponding angle is $70^{\circ}$, and angle $x$ is the corresponding angle at $m$.

Which claim correctly finds $x$ and what it shows about $\ell$ and $m$?

options.A: Call the answer the words parallel lines, and stop there.
options.B: Say equal corresponding angles are what create transversal $t$.
options.C: $x = 70^{\circ}$, and the equal corresponding angles show $\ell \parallel m$ on that page.
options.D: Settle $x$ by requiring a shared perpendicular to $\ell$ and $m$, not corresponding angles from $t$.
